title: Creation visual catalogue
status: Authored production specification; not an image review or recognition verdict

source.snapshotScope: The full manuscript bytes at semantic authorship, before production presentation metadata. The digest remains attached to that version; recipe line numbers refer to it. Validation separately checks current identities, recipes and chapter contexts, so artwork-only edits need not replace this provenance.

direction.name: Celestial atlas in luminous gouache and ink
direction.status: Provisionally adopted luminous gouache/lapis-circle direction; production catalogue remains subject to image-level review
direction.presentation: Every identity, including fixed locations and abstract capabilities, is a circular symbolic painted token: a window onto a phenomenon, population or activity, never a literally portable universe. One fine restrained ivory-gold rim encloses each token, with transparent exterior and generous breathing room inside.
direction.technique: Broad opaque gouache shapes with luminous layered washes, economical dark ink contours, strong small-scale silhouettes and sparse textured detail. Keep identifying anatomy and large spatial relations visible at play size.
prohibitions: No printed words, letters, numbers, question marks or music staffs in artwork.
No modern books, laboratory gear, batteries, scientific instruments or classroom furniture.
No decorative astrolabes, alchemical glyphs, religious symbols or invented interfaces.
No tiny diagrams whose meaning depends on reading fine marks.
No buildings or settlements as the dominant image.

recognitionProtocol.prospectiveFor: Reviews begun after this catalogue snapshot. Freeze the acceptable classes before presenting images.
recognitionProtocol.priorFeedbackKnownToAuthor: The production lead supplied pilot feedback during authorship: pure circular giant footprints were mistaken for craters, and song/memory/change distinctions remain context-assisted. These criteria must not be used to retroactively score those earlier pilot passes.
recognitionProtocol.exact: Blind response should name the depicted thing or an ordinary semantic equivalent. Allowed responses are listed before images are reviewed.
recognitionProtocol.family: Blind response may identify the correct object or phenomenon family; the exact historical stage or story label is supplied by ordinary names and chapter context.
recognitionProtocol.contextAssisted: The unlabelled image must communicate the listed physical subject or convention. The exact capability, causal claim or temporal state is judged only after ordinary chapter context is supplied; a blind family match must not be reported as exact semantic recognition.
recognitionProtocol.scoring: Use listed acceptableBlindMatches as semantic answer classes, not exact string matching. Capture first guess, alternatives and confidence before revealing names. Do not expand acceptable classes after seeing responses without recording a new prospective review. Neighbor confusion is recorded separately from family match.
recognitionProtocol.nameAvailability: In play the name appears on creation, hover, press, drag and keyboard focus; a fixed hotspot also retains its name. Context-assisted recognition is intentional, not a claim of icon-only comprehension.
recognitionProtocol.evidenceLimit: This catalogue authors intended subjects and prospective acceptance criteria; it provides no human recognition, preference, learning or enjoyment evidence.

continuity.planet: Use one non-Earth world throughout: an ochre hook-shaped primary landmass with two short satellite ridges and a jade sea. Do not copy Earth continents.
continuity.moon: Use one pale ivory Moon. Close views retain a neighboring pair of round craters by the lower lit edge; phases vary while the round body persists.
continuity.coastAndCave: The same hooked ochre-grey cliff begins as solid, unbroken mineral rock. Tidal shore in c04 has no cave or arch; Coastal mosaic and Living coast in c10 also retain an unbroken cliff because the independent Sea cave combination may occur later in that chapter. Waves plus Stone crust creates the wave-cut opening in c10. From Sea cave onward preserve that opening at the waterline, a sloped dry upper ledge and a pale inner wall above ordinary tidal wash through cave, painting and music scenes.
continuity.greatBrowsers: Long-necked sauropod-like reptiles with pillar legs and small heads. Their trackway uses large oval hind depressions with smaller clawless horseshoe/D-shaped foreprints; Last tracks and Fossil footprints preserve exactly two alternating step pairs, four impressions total, with identical spacing and orientation in fresh wet mud versus a dry layered stone slab. Avoid generic crater circles. After Last tracks, show only tracks, fossils, absence or a clearly depicted memory/painting; never living returned giants.
continuity.mammalAncestry: Pre-impact small mammals have pointed noses, round ears, long tails and ochre fur. Survivors and cold-coat variation keep those anchors; later mammal branches preserve mammalian anatomy without implying an instant transformation of one individual.
continuity.flightBranches: Insects have six legs and membranous insect wings, birds have feathers and two hind feet, bats have fur and finger-supported skin wings. No shared silhouette that suggests one branch became another.
continuity.microbiology: Painted atlas magnification is a symbolic convention without microscopes or lab hardware. Early cells have simple internal threads and grains, not a compulsory nucleus; partnered cells show an independently bounded internal partner.
continuity.soundAndMemory: Simple broad sound arcs carry animal calls and human song; reflection reverses an arc at a cave wall. A faint repeated outline indicates memory. The inherited song uses two ivory arcs plus a third; its changed ending rises in coral. These conventions need contextual review, not invented claims of universal recognition.
continuity.humans: Use small expressive human silhouettes with varied ages and natural skin tones within the palette, simple undetailed wraps where needed, and readable hands and gaze. Keep primate-like tree dwellers in c23 distinct from the human community conventions in c24 onward; the myth compresses this passage.
continuity.earlyLand: Before Shore plants in c11, above-water land in landscape tokens is strictly bare ochre-grey rock, gravel or sediment: no green tufts, grass, moss, roots, bushes or trees. In c10 Coastal mosaic and Living coast, green life is confined to kelp and algae visibly below the water surface; coral is also underwater. Rain falls onto cool solid grey crust, never glowing lava. These constraints take precedence over vegetation or an early cave accidentally present in historical reference atlases.

chapters.name: Let there be somewhere
chapters.intro:
You have no throne, no worshippers, and nowhere to stand. Only Earth, Air, Fire and Water: matter, motion, energy and change.

This is a creation myth. Your gestures can span a billion years; they are not laboratory recipes. Make something worth looking at.

chapters.name: The gift inside a star
chapters.intro: A star can shine for ages and still have a last day. Let one of your great lights change what the universe can be made of.

chapters.name: A restless world
chapters.intro: Choose one young sun among the many. Around it, give the scattered matter somewhere to gather—and an interior that will refuse to sit still.

chapters.name: A companion and a shore
chapters.intro: Another body crosses the young world's path. Let the meeting remake the sky, then give the cooling planet a sea.

chapters.name: Water learns the way home
chapters.intro: A full ocean is a beginning. Lift its water into the sky and see where the land sends it back.

chapters.name: The stone is not finished
chapters.intro: The solid face looks permanent from a shore. Beneath it, heat is still moving the world.

chapters.name: The first inside
chapters.intro: The ocean contains ingredients and energy, but no one is alive. Here your myth must cross a gap that science has not yet explained: give matter an inside that can keep itself going.

chapters.name: A dangerous new sky
chapters.intro: The sun-fed cells release a gas. What is waste to one kind of life can become power—or poison—to another.

chapters.name: More than a single cell
chapters.intro: An inside can shelter partners. Now let cells stay together and discover what a body can do.

chapters.name: Cities without streets
chapters.intro: You could fill the sea with isolated creatures. Instead, make places where one life becomes shelter for another.

chapters.name: The bare continents
chapters.intro: From above, the continents are enormous and almost empty. Bring life across the wet margin without pretending dry stone is already soil.

chapters.name: Nothing lives on light alone
chapters.intro: The forest grows, and the ground fills with what it sheds. Give the fallen material somewhere to go.

chapters.name: Small wings over a continent
chapters.intro: The forest offers leaves, food and shelter. Let a small branch of animal life explore the spaces between them.

chapters.name: The shore is crossed again
chapters.intro: The land has food and shelter, but living there asks new things of a body. Let different branches of animal life find different ways across.

chapters.name: A bargain in colour
chapters.intro: A plant cannot walk to a mate or carry its offspring far away. Let it make offers that other lives have reasons to accept.

chapters.name: One sun, many worlds
chapters.intro: The same sunlight reaches a world of unequal heights and uneven rain. Give life places that ask different things of it.

chapters.name: Hunger belongs here too
chapters.intro: Abundance does not mean that every creature can live without eating another. Connect feeding, waste and new growth across the grassland.

chapters.name: The long journeys
chapters.intro: Life can leave the place where it began. Give creatures ways to cross distance, and let separation change what their descendants become.

chapters.name: What the sky takes back
chapters.intro: Not every remnant of planet-building has found a quiet orbit. The gravity that gathered your world can also bring a catastrophe. Keep a trace of what this world is about to lose.

chapters.name: Life in the dark
chapters.intro: The giants' paths have fallen silent. Among the fallen trees, look for lives that can endure without the old abundance.

chapters.name: A different green
chapters.intro: Light returns. New feet cross the giants' old paths; help surviving lives meet one another in a changed forest.

chapters.name: When the ice advances
chapters.intro: Ages pass. The cold heights have kept their glaciers. Now long changes in climate favour snow that survives the summer. As the ice spreads, give different lives more than one way through it.

chapters.name: Yesterday inside a creature
chapters.intro: Look closely at one community among the branches. Let its members remember a place and share a warning before another animal reaches it.

chapters.name: The sky looks back
chapters.intro: A creature looks up at the night sky. Give it a way to ask about the lights—and a way to test an answer.

chapters.name: Things you did not imagine
chapters.intro: Return to the sea cave your waves carved long ago. Its dry walls can hold an image; its chambers can send a voice back.

chapters.name: The next verse
chapters.intro: Listen to what a new generation does with an old song.

chapters.name: The hand opens
chapters.intro: You can still move mountains. Watch instead where a seed goes next.

chapters.name: The End
chapters.intro:
The stars have not stopped forging elements. Water is still finding the sea. Somewhere, a creature is learning a song you have never heard.

You began with four gifts. You leave a world that can give.

entries.name: Earth
entries.visualSubject: An angular ochre chunk of mineral matter with exposed dark strata and a few dense crumbs, isolated against ultramarine. Its solid, weighty silhouette stands for the primal power of matter.
entries.distinction: A compact mineral mass, without roots, globe outline, wet paint or organic topsoil.

entries.name: Air
entries.visualSubject: Three broad ivory ribbons of moving air curl around a clear central opening, with a few tiny wind-carried grains at the outer turn. Leave most of the circle open.
entries.distinction: Open directional flow with no cloud body, suspended veil or liquid surface.

entries.name: Fire
entries.visualSubject: One compact coral flame with a pale hot heart and two broad upward tongues, hovering in darkness without logs or a hearth.
entries.distinction: Flame silhouette rather than a ray, round celestial disk or erupting mountain.

entries.name: Water
entries.visualSubject: One heavy jade-blue droplet leans into a short curling pool, with a clear pale highlight and deep transparent belly.
entries.distinction: A simple liquid emblem rather than a seascape, wave train or cloud.

entries.name: Light
entries.visualSubject: A single brilliant ivory point releases a broad diagonal beam through ultramarine darkness; the beam visibly opens into empty space.
entries.distinction: Dominant ray and point, with no spherical stellar surface, flame tongues or field of separate stars.

entries.name: Dust
entries.visualSubject: A loose diagonal spray of small dry ochre grains and uneven flakes, with individual particles separated by dark space.
entries.distinction: Sparse plain grains; enriched dust has varied reflective inclusions, sediment has settled layers, dense cloud has a coherent body.

entries.name: Mist
entries.visualSubject: A low, translucent jade-white veil folds into two soft overlapping wisps, with dark background still visible through its body.
entries.distinction: Soft transparent veil rather than a solid cloud bank, dry grains or open ribbon-shaped wind.

entries.name: Gravity
entries.visualSubject: Three unequal rocky spheres lie along narrowing curved paths toward one larger dark sphere; the nearest small sphere is visibly closest to the large mass. Keep the paths fine and the masses prominent.
entries.distinction: Convergence toward one mass; no symmetric magnetic loops, flat disk or tipped globe axis.

entries.name: Dense cloud
entries.visualSubject: A compact indigo and jade cosmic cloud has a very dark dense knot at its centre and pale granular edges folded inward. No star shines inside it yet.
entries.distinction: One dark unlit knot, distinct from diffuse mist, a nursery with multiple bright embryos and an illuminated remnant.

entries.name: First star
entries.visualSubject: One white-blue spherical star shines alone in a nearly empty ultramarine field, with a restrained pale halo and no flame-like surface.
entries.distinction: Small solitary cool-white disk; the Sun is ochre, the massive star fills much more of its token and light is a beam.

entries.name: Starfield
entries.visualSubject: A loose irregular scatter of separate ivory and warm-white stars occupies the circle, with clear dark gaps and no connecting lines.
entries.distinction: Dispersed independent lights rather than a spiral, a connected pattern or marks on stone.

entries.name: Galaxy
entries.visualSubject: A tilted spiral galaxy has two broad luminous arms, granular star clouds, dark dust lanes and a small bright central bulge.
entries.distinction: Recognizable spiral arms made of many lights, not a smooth ring around one sun.

entries.name: Massive star
entries.visualSubject: An enormous blue-white stellar disk fills most of the circle, its intensely bright limb surrounded by a thick hot halo. Preserve the rounded surface and avoid tongues of fire.
entries.distinction: Much greater visual weight and hotter hue than the solitary first star; no exposed interior.

entries.name: Fusing core
entries.visualSubject: A cutaway of a luminous star exposes a small white central core nested inside three broad coral and ochre shells, with tiny paired grains becoming denser clusters in the innermost shell.
entries.distinction: Stellar shell cutaway with luminous fusion centre, not a rocky planetary shell or released grains.

entries.name: Supernova
entries.visualSubject: A fierce white central flash throws broad coral ejecta fingers outward in every direction, with torn stellar layers visibly separating from the centre.
entries.distinction: Active radial stellar explosion without a colliding globe, landscape or settled hollow shell.

entries.name: Heavy elements
entries.visualSubject: Within a dark cutaway wedge of stellar material, several compact clusters of ivory, coral and metallic ochre grains sit tightly packed, enclosed by a curved glowing stellar shell. This is an atlas convention for heavier nuclei still inside a star.
entries.distinction: Dense grain clusters contained in stellar material; no molecular chains, dust spray or planetary metal sphere.

entries.name: Expanding remnant
entries.visualSubject: A broad hollow shell of ragged coral gas surrounds a dark evacuated centre, with sparse fragments continuing outward beyond its rim. The initial blinding flash has passed.
entries.distinction: Empty centre and expanding shell rather than a bright explosion centre or soft illuminated cloud.

entries.name: Glowing nebula
entries.visualSubject: Filmy jade and coral gas folds glow across a dark central opening, edged with delicate ivory light and a few embedded points. The cloud is thin and luminous rather than solid.
entries.distinction: Soft illuminated filaments, without the remnant's enclosing shell or nursery's dense bright knots.

entries.name: Enriched dust
entries.visualSubject: A diagonal cloud of fine dark grains contains larger ochre, coral and pale metallic flecks, all dispersed freely against deep blue. Several flecks show distinct bright edges.
entries.distinction: A mixed diffuse spray of enriched material; plain Dust lacks the contrasting inclusions, Heavy elements remain enclosed in a star.

entries.name: New stellar nursery
entries.visualSubject: Three compact white-gold star embryos glow inside separate dense folds of one large jade and ultramarine cloud, with fine ochre grains gathered around them.
entries.distinction: Multiple embedded bright knots connected by dense dusty folds; not an unlit cloud or exposed stars.

entries.name: Sun
entries.visualSubject: A warm ochre sun with a pale circular face and a short clean corona floats in dark blue space; its disk is calm and complete.
entries.distinction: Warm gold disk of moderate size, without flame tongues or the massive star's nearly full-frame blue-white glare.

entries.name: Planetary disk
entries.visualSubject: A small golden sun sits inside a broad flat tilted disk of dusty ochre rings, with a clear central opening and scattered clumps along the disk.
entries.distinction: One central star and a smooth accretion plane rather than spiral arms of stars or converging bodies.

entries.name: Planetesimals
entries.visualSubject: Four irregular rocky bodies of different sizes tumble together in empty blue space; the largest has a rough cratered edge and none is spherical.
entries.distinction: A few substantial irregular stones with dark gaps; no dust haze, completed globe or active collision.

entries.name: Rocky world
entries.visualSubject: A solid round young planet has a dark ochre surface with the same hook-shaped raised landmass and two small satellite ridges used throughout this world, against deep blue space. No familiar Earth continent is present.
entries.distinction: Whole round planet with recurring non-Earth landform; crust is a close cross-section, continent is a flat coastal view.

entries.name: Magma ocean
entries.visualSubject: The same round planet glows coral across most of its surface; a few dark cooling rafts outline the hooked landmass as cracks of bright molten rock divide them.
entries.distinction: Planet-wide molten surface rather than a cool globe, crust slice or single volcanic mountain.

entries.name: Iron core
entries.visualSubject: A rocky planet is cut open to show a dense ochre-metal inner sphere surrounded by a broad coral liquid-metal layer and a thinner dark rocky mantle.
entries.distinction: Dense planetary metal centre inside rocky shells; no stellar glow, nuclear grain clusters or exterior field loops.

entries.name: Magnetic field
entries.visualSubject: The recurring dark planet is enclosed by two large symmetric jade field loops that leave one pole and curve back to the other, with a few solar particles diverted around the outside.
entries.distinction: Paired loops around poles; gravity paths converge on a mass, aurora is confined to a polar sky and tilt has one straight axis.

entries.name: Stone crust
entries.visualSubject: A broad curved slab of dark solid rock shows a cool cracked upper surface and a thin coral glow beneath its cut edge, suggesting a hardened skin over a hot interior.
entries.distinction: One intact hardened shell section; Earth is a compact raw chunk, moving plates are distinct slabs at a boundary.

entries.name: Aurora
entries.visualSubject: Tall jade and pale-coral curtains hang above a dark curved polar horizon, their lower edges rippling while a few small stars remain visible overhead.
entries.distinction: Vertical glowing night curtains over one pole, without full globe loops, a daylight bow or layered atmosphere.

entries.name: Giant impact
entries.visualSubject: An oblique small rocky body strikes the rim of the recurring large planet, sending a white-coral fan of debris into a curved orbit while most of the planet remains intact.
entries.distinction: Visible collision between unequal bodies and an orbiting debris fan; impact winter shows the later darkened world.

entries.name: Moon
entries.visualSubject: A pale ivory moon combines a clearly lit crescent with its faint round unlit body; two neighboring circular craters sit near the lit lower edge. Retain that crater pair in every close Moon view.
entries.distinction: Pale crescent with identifiable paired craters, not a star, colored world or sequence of phases.

entries.name: Tides
entries.visualSubject: The hooked shore appears in miniature under the pale Moon; two broad nested waterlines show the sea at high and low positions against the same rock.
entries.distinction: Two water levels visibly associated with a Moon; tidal shore emphasizes exposed habitat and lunar rhythm includes multiple phases.

entries.name: First rain
entries.visualSubject: Large bright raindrops fall from a low grey-white cloud onto cool, solid grey stone, making pale splashes and small dark wet patches on its closed, unlit cracks. All land is bare mineral rock; there is no molten lava, fire, orange glow or vegetation.
entries.distinction: Rain reaches hardened cool grey crust that can hold liquid water, with no lava or glowing cracks; Rainfall later shows a wider bare hillside and connected stream.

acceptableBlindMatches: first rain on a barren world
rain falling onto solid grey stone

entries.name: Rain-filled hollows
entries.visualSubject: Three irregular shallow basins in bare dark stone hold separate jade pools beneath the last few raindrops; raised dry rock clearly divides the pools.
entries.distinction: Distinct water-filled depressions on barren crust, before connected sea or vegetation.

entries.name: Ocean
entries.visualSubject: A broad uninterrupted ultramarine sea curves toward a quiet pale horizon, with one deep jade foreground swell and no visible islands or living shore.
entries.distinction: Expansive connected sea rather than a droplet, a breaking wave sequence or exposed coastal shelf.

entries.name: Tidal shore
entries.visualSubject: A shallow jade sea recedes from a solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey cliff, exposing a broad wet mineral shelf dotted with small tide pools. The cliff has no cave, arch or opening, and every exposed land surface is bare rock or sediment without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.
entries.distinction: Exposed tidal shelf and pools beside an unbroken mineral cliff; no cave before its later creation, terrestrial vegetation, rich habitat mosaic or tidal double diagram.

entries.name: Evaporation
entries.visualSubject: A warm ochre sun illuminates a shallow sea, where thin transparent streams rise from the surface and fade into clear air before forming any cloud.
entries.distinction: Upward movement off a lit water surface, no droplet cloud; pale streams are a process convention, not visible water vapour.

acceptableBlindMatches: water rising from a sunlit sea

entries.name: Clouds
entries.visualSubject: Two substantial ivory cumulus clouds stack softly above a flat dark lower edge, with cool jade shadows and a few pale gaps between the lobes.
entries.distinction: Opaque terrestrial cloud masses without falling rain, cosmic dust or low translucent veil.

entries.name: Rainfall
entries.visualSubject: A broad grey-jade cloud releases a visible curtain of slanting pale drops onto a bare ochre-grey mineral hillside and a small jade stream. Smooth rock slopes, loose sediment and rain-darkened stone carry no green tufts, grass, roots, moss or trees.
entries.distinction: Ordinary rain over strictly barren mineral land, without glowing crust, vegetation, forest canopy or snow crystals.

entries.name: Rivers
entries.visualSubject: One strong jade river winds from high grey hills across bare ochre mineral land, fed by two narrow tributaries that merge into its single channel. Exposed banks and hills consist entirely of rock, gravel and sediment, with no green tufts, grass, roots or trees.
entries.distinction: Tributaries converge into one main flow over barren mineral terrain; braided channels repeatedly divide and rejoin, while Delta splits toward the sea.

entries.name: Sediment
entries.visualSubject: A low fan of sorted ochre sand, pale pebbles and dark fine silt lies in shallow water, with visibly separate coarse and fine bands along its edge.
entries.distinction: Water-laid loose grains rather than airborne dust, root-rich soil or hardened striped rock.

entries.name: Delta
entries.visualSubject: A jade river splits into three outward-reaching channels across a triangular ochre sediment fan at the edge of a dark blue sea. Every bar, bank and upstream slope is bare ochre-grey mineral material, with no green tufts, grass, roots, marsh plants or trees.
entries.distinction: Distributary branches fan into the sea across bare mineral sediment; no vegetation, single trunk valley or inland loops.

entries.name: Rainbow
entries.visualSubject: One bright but restrained multicolored bow arcs between a sunlit cloud edge and a slanting rain shower, with dark blue space inside the curve.
entries.distinction: Smooth ordered daylight color arc rather than curtains, field loops or circulating process.

entries.name: Water cycle
entries.visualSubject: A compact island cross-section shows a sunlit sea, a cloud above a bare grey-ochre mountain and a jade river returning to the same sea, joined by one pale sweeping loop rising on the sea side and descending over land. Every above-water surface is exposed rock or sediment, without green tufts, grass, roots or trees.
entries.distinction: The connected sea-cloud-bare-land-return arrangement remains legible without vegetation, words or flowchart boxes; it does not show forest transpiration.

acceptableBlindMatches: water circulating between sea sky and land

entries.name: Moving plates
entries.visualSubject: Two thick dark crustal slabs meet in cutaway: one bends downward beneath the other while a coral seam opens at the far side. Broad pale motion strokes follow the slabs.
entries.distinction: Multiple moving slabs and two boundary actions, not an isolated trench or static hardened crust.

entries.name: Continent
entries.visualSubject: A broad ochre landmass with the world's distinctive hook-shaped cape stretches across a jade sea, its inland ridges low and its coastline continuous.
entries.distinction: Broad connected land seen obliquely, without globe outline, isolated cone or close tidal shelf.

entries.name: Trench
entries.visualSubject: A side cutaway beneath a continuous blue ocean shows a narrow seafloor trough where the left rocky plate bends downward and continues diagonally beneath the neighboring right plate. Keep the descending slab visibly continuous below its neighbor within solid ochre-grey mantle, with only a narrow water-filled surface depression rather than a giant open fissure.
entries.distinction: A narrow subduction trench with a continuous slab descending beneath its neighbor; no giant open crack, empty canyon, land valley, vegetation or smoking chimney.

entries.name: Volcano
entries.visualSubject: A steep dark volcanic cone releases a compact coral eruption and a short glowing lava stream down one flank, with an exposed crater at the summit.
entries.distinction: Land cone and crater dominate, without surrounding ocean horizon, seafloor vent plume or incoming body.

entries.name: Hydrothermal vent
entries.visualSubject: Two rough dark mineral chimneys rise from the deep seafloor, releasing thick black plumes into jade water; small pale mineral edges catch the faint light.
entries.distinction: Underwater chimneys with dark plumes, not an erupting cone, trench or diagram of microscopic chemistry.

entries.name: Weathered rock
entries.visualSubject: A large ochre rock is split by water-darkened cracks, with rounded corners, detached chips and a short rivulet carrying fine grains away from its base.
entries.distinction: Visible rock breaking down and material leaving it; no organic roots or already settled sediment fan.

entries.name: Mineral-rich sea
entries.visualSubject: At a rocky coast, a jade river plume fans into blue sea carrying a few bright mineral grains that grow smaller and fade into the water. Show the moving water and mineral source together.
entries.distinction: Dissolving material enters a coastal water plume; no pile of crystals, laboratory vessel or claim that dissolved ions remain visible.

acceptableBlindMatches: river delivering minerals to the ocean

entries.name: Volcanic island
entries.visualSubject: A bare dark volcanic island rises from a broad blue sea, with a small ochre crater and fresh black lava slopes reaching directly into the water.
entries.distinction: Isolated ocean-surrounded cone with no plants or animals; eruption is secondary to new island shape.

entries.name: Organic molecules
entries.visualSubject: Several irregular chains and small loops of joined ochre, ivory and coral grains drift in dark jade water beside one mineral surface. Use a hand-painted microscopic atlas convention, without letters, bonds as technical diagrams or equipment.
entries.distinction: Loose varied connected chains, not dense nuclear clusters, sun-energized compact packets or enclosing membranes.

entries.name: Membranes
entries.visualSubject: Two thin translucent jade bubbles float in dark water, each with a clear double-edged boundary enclosing nearly empty fluid; one open curved sheet is folding toward closure.
entries.distinction: Simple empty flexible boundaries without internal living structures, division or hard shell ridges.

entries.name: Chemical fuel
entries.visualSubject: A small cluster of tightly joined coral and ochre molecular grains catches a narrow shaft of sunlight, with warm light retained in the cluster after the beam passes. Keep a few unlit grains nearby for contrast.
entries.distinction: A molecular energy-storage convention, with no flame, battery, fuel can or suggestion of food being oxygen.

entries.name: Living cell
entries.visualSubject: One large soft jade cell has a clearly bounded outer membrane and a few small internal coral threads and grains suspended in fluid. Keep the interior simple, with no prominent nucleus.
entries.distinction: One inhabited cellular boundary, not an empty vesicle, dividing pair or large host containing a distinct internal partner.

entries.name: Dividing cells
entries.visualSubject: Two matching jade cell lobes pinch apart through a narrow connecting waist, each containing the same small coral thread-and-grain pattern.
entries.distinction: A clear division neck between two inherited near-matches; colonies are a larger attached group and variation shows several differing descendants.

entries.name: Variation
entries.visualSubject: Four related jade cells form a loose branching family, sharing the same basic boundary but differing slightly in size and in the arrangement of their coral internal threads.
entries.distinction: Small inherited differences among related cells, without a division waist or animal coat differences.

entries.name: Sun-fed cells
entries.visualSubject: Three jade-green cells lie close beneath a warm shaft of sunlight, their interiors filled with small leaf-green granules; a few pale bubbles leave the group.
entries.distinction: Sunlit microbial group with green granules, not a leafy sea plant or a cell taking oxygen inward.

entries.name: Microbial mats
entries.visualSubject: A low emerald and ochre living film coats a flat wet rock, shown with one cut edge revealing several thin soft layers; tiny bubbles sit along its surface.
entries.distinction: Flat microbial carpet rather than domed stone structures, leafy moss or a protected underside close-up.

entries.name: Stromatolites
entries.visualSubject: Three rounded low domes rise in shallow water, their cutaway sides revealing closely stacked wavy ochre and jade laminae beneath a thin living green surface.
entries.distinction: Built domed laminated structures, not flat mats, straight iron bands or branching animal skeletons.

entries.name: Oxygen
entries.visualSubject: Several pale paired spheres rise as bubbles from a small green microbial patch in water, with one pair enlarged near the foreground. The repeated pair is a simple atlas convention for oxygen.
entries.distinction: Paired gas motif arising from living water; ozone uses triads high around a planet and sky shows accumulated atmosphere.

entries.name: Rusted seabed
entries.visualSubject: A shallow seabed is stained with broad coral-red and dark ochre deposits, with a thin greenish water layer and a few settling pale particles above it.
entries.distinction: Loose rust-colored deposits under water, without hardened repeating stripes or prepared pigment puddles.

entries.name: Banded iron
entries.visualSubject: A broken upright slab exposes bold alternating dark iron-grey and coral-red horizontal bands, with a rough outer edge and a small wet seabed base.
entries.distinction: Repeated hard contrasting mineral stripes, without loose mud, one black carbon seam or shell impressions.

entries.name: Oxygen-rich sky
entries.visualSubject: The familiar hooked continent curves beneath a broad clear pale-blue atmospheric band, containing a few paired ivory gas marks well above the sea.
entries.distinction: Broad lower atmosphere around the world; ozone is a separate thin high cap and oxygen alone is bubbles above microbes.

entries.name: Ozone layer
entries.visualSubject: A thin luminous jade shell lies high above the familiar curved planet, with three-part pale gas clusters and several short incoming violet light rays fading at the shell.
entries.distinction: Thin high atmospheric shield absorbing rays; no broad low gas band, symmetric magnetic loops or polar curtains.

entries.name: Oxygen-using cells
entries.visualSubject: One pale jade cell draws paired ivory gas marks inward beside a separate small ochre food grain; its simple interior shows a warm coral glow.
entries.distinction: Oxygen and a separate food particle enter the cell, without sunlight or a distinct engulfed partner.

entries.name: Partnered cells
entries.visualSubject: A large translucent jade host cell encloses one clearly distinct small coral oval partner with a folded internal line; both retain visible boundaries.
entries.distinction: A cell within a cell, not merely adjacent cells, an empty membrane or a generic nucleus.

entries.name: Sheltered microbes
entries.visualSubject: A lifted corner of a thick green microbial mat reveals a dark sealed pocket in the underlying mud, containing several tiny pale cells protected beneath the living surface.
entries.distinction: Microbes beneath an oxygen-excluding mud-and-mat roof, not exposed surface growth, wood shelter or free bubbles.

entries.name: Cell colonies
entries.visualSubject: A loose rosette of eight visibly separate jade cells touches edge to edge, each cell retaining its own outline and simple interior.
entries.distinction: Many similar cells loosely joined, without a differentiated continuous body or a host enclosing a partner.

entries.name: Multicellular life
entries.visualSubject: A simple rounded ribbon-shaped body is assembled from two visibly different sizes of connected cells, with one continuous outer contour and a hollow central passage.
entries.distinction: Integrated differentiated cellular body rather than a loose rosette, recognizable animal or leafy alga.

entries.name: Algae
entries.visualSubject: A small rooted-looking but unattached cluster of jade and olive seaweed fronds grows from a rough submerged stone; broad translucent blades bend underwater.
entries.distinction: One low seaweed cluster with no woody stem, terrestrial leaves or animal tentacles.

entries.name: Soft-bodied animals
entries.visualSubject: A translucent oval marine animal with a gently lobed edge rests beside a slender worm-like companion; both have soft continuous bodies without hard shells or jointed legs.
entries.distinction: Soft simple animal bodies, distinct from a streamlined swimmer, armored jointed limbs or attached polyps.

entries.name: Swimming animals
entries.visualSubject: A streamlined small marine animal swims diagonally, propelled by broad side fins and a clearly flexed tail, with a simple head and no emphasized eye.
entries.distinction: Active fish-like swimmer entirely underwater, without surfacing breath, mammal flippers or passive soft body shapes.

entries.name: Eyes
entries.visualSubject: A close view of a small marine animal's head gives one large dark eye a bright highlight, while a narrow shaft of light reaches the eye from above.
entries.distinction: Eye structure and incoming light dominate; no primate gaze or night-adapted pair of eyes.

entries.name: Shells
entries.visualSubject: Two hard pale marine shells sit against deep jade water: one strong spiral and one ribbed fan shape, both visibly hollow at the opening.
entries.distinction: Separate hard shell structures without an enclosing rock impression, embryo or translucent film.

entries.name: Fossils
entries.visualSubject: A split ochre stone slab reveals a sharply outlined spiral-shell impression and a small ribbed shell trace embedded in the rock.
entries.distinction: Shell evidence inside stone, not loose living shells or giant rounded track impressions.

entries.name: Kelp forest
entries.visualSubject: Three tall ochre-jade kelp stems rise from dark submerged rocks, bearing long ribbon blades and a few round gas floats beneath a pale water surface.
entries.distinction: Tall underwater canopy of kelp with holdfasts and floats; no land trunks or highlighted juvenile swimmers.

entries.name: Coral
entries.visualSubject: One small colony of pale coral polyps attaches to a submerged stone, each polyp an open cup with a short crown of tentacles.
entries.distinction: Soft animal polyps are prominent; no vast hard reef architecture or plant-like frond.

entries.name: Reef partnership
entries.visualSubject: One enlarged coral polyp shows a pale translucent body containing several small jade-green cells; its tentacles remain spread above a rough attachment stone.
entries.distinction: Algal cells visibly within a recognizable coral animal, not merely near it or inside an unrelated cell.

entries.name: Coral reef
entries.visualSubject: A compact underwater reef combines several sturdy branching and mound-shaped pale coral skeletons, with tiny living coral tips and deep blue gaps between the structures.
entries.distinction: Large built calcium-carbonate architecture rather than a close polyp, tall kelp or broad multiple-habitat map.

entries.name: Nursery waters
entries.visualSubject: Three tiny jade juvenile swimmers shelter within a protective arch of large ochre kelp blades, their small bodies sharply silhouetted in a calm dark gap.
entries.distinction: Young animals visibly sheltered by much larger kelp, not a plain kelp stand or independent swimming group.

entries.name: Coastal mosaic
entries.visualSubject: An oblique strip of solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast contains separate cool dark kelp coves and warmer pale coral shallows, divided by bare rocky headlands and connected by blue water. All green kelp and algae remain visibly underwater; exposed land has no green tufts, grass, roots or trees, and the cliff has no cave or arch.
entries.distinction: Spatially separated marine habitats beside strictly bare mineral land; no premature shore plants or cave. Living coast additionally emphasizes tidal exchange and an exposed shelf.

entries.name: Living coast
entries.visualSubject: The solid unbroken hooked ochre-grey coast holds a submerged kelp cove, separate underwater coral shallows and a broad bare tidal shelf; one sweeping jade tidal current connects the habitats around the cape. Green life is confined to visibly underwater kelp and algae, while all exposed land remains mineral without green tufts, grass, roots, trees, cave or arch.
entries.distinction: Rich marine habitats connected by tidal exchange beside bare land, with kelp and coral in separate submerged coves; no terrestrial vegetation or cave that may not yet have been made.

entries.name: Waves
entries.visualSubject: Three broad jade ocean swells approach in diagonal succession, the nearest curling into a clear ivory breaking crest over dark water.
entries.distinction: Rhythmic moving crests dominate, without a droplet, Moon or high-low shore comparison.

entries.name: Sea cave
entries.visualSubject: A close oblique view of the same hooked cliff shows a dark wave-cut entrance at water level, a sloping dry upper ledge and a pale unmarked inner wall above the wash.
entries.distinction: One identifiable coastal cave and dry wall, without paint, singers or a different inland cavern.

entries.name: Shore plants
entries.visualSubject: Small upright green shoots and flat primitive-looking leaflets occupy wet cracks just above a jade shoreline, with algae still visible below the waterline.
entries.distinction: Transitional wet-margin land growth, not fully submerged seaweed, a dense moss cushion or isolated underground roots.

acceptableBlindMatches: plants growing at the water's edge

entries.name: Soil
entries.visualSubject: A compact cutaway of dark crumbly topsoil shows pale fine roots, decomposed leaf fragments and scattered mineral grains beneath a thin green surface.
entries.distinction: Organic crumb structure and roots distinguish living soil from raw mineral matter, sorted sediment and soaked plant layers.

entries.name: Windblown spores
entries.visualSubject: Fine pale spore grains blow from a small open capsule on a slender green stalk, spreading into a broad tapering trail above low wet growth.
entries.distinction: Minute unwinged reproductive grains from a capsule; no seed bodies, wings or embryo stores.

entries.name: Moss
entries.visualSubject: A dense low cushion of bright jade moss carries several fine upright stalks with tiny brown capsules, rooted against a wet dark stone.
entries.distinction: Soft leafy cushion and capsule stalks, not a flat microbial film or large divided fronds.

entries.name: Wetland
entries.visualSubject: A shallow dark pool lies among low mossy hummocks and saturated ochre ground, with several small patches of standing water connected below the growth.
entries.distinction: Waterlogged low vegetation without sea waves, desert sand or tall dry grasses.

entries.name: Roots
entries.visualSubject: One sturdy green stem ends in a spreading fan of pale branching roots, revealed in a dark soil cutaway with fine rootlets reaching toward water pockets.
entries.distinction: Root architecture is the main silhouette, not a soil sample, frond or moving nutrient flecks.

entries.name: Ferns
entries.visualSubject: Two large jade fern fronds unfurl above a small dark root mass; one curled fiddlehead stands beside a fully opened divided frond.
entries.distinction: Familiar divided frond and curled new growth, no flowers, woody crowns or capsule-covered moss cushion.

entries.name: First forest
entries.visualSubject: Three tall primitive tree-fern-like trunks rise from wet ground into spreading divided jade crowns, with low ferns beneath and no flowers, fruit or animals.
entries.distinction: Tall wet spore-bearing forest with clear bare trunks; later forests add nutrient cycling, flowers or young recovery growth.

entries.name: Fallen wood
entries.visualSubject: One thick broken dark branch lies diagonally, its pale torn end and a few attached bark strips clearly visible against a small patch of leaf litter.
entries.distinction: Single intact dead branch, without landscape devastation, fungal breakdown or sheltering animals.

entries.name: Fungi
entries.visualSubject: A small group of ochre and ivory mushrooms grows from a dark fallen branch, with pale threadlike mycelium exposed beneath one lifted bark edge.
entries.distinction: Fungal caps and mycelial threads are both present, not leafy growth, marine polyps or a crumbling log scene.

entries.name: Decomposition
entries.visualSubject: A broken log crumbles into dark fibrous fragments beneath pale fungal threads and two small mushroom caps; the intact end transitions visibly into loose organic matter.
entries.distinction: Active material breakdown across the log, not fungi alone or already released nutrients entering roots.

entries.name: Returned nutrients
entries.visualSubject: Small ochre and pale mineral flecks emerge from dark decomposed leaf fragments and gather beside fine roots in moist soil, following a short pale flow through the cutaway.
entries.distinction: Nutrient return into root-bearing soil, not simply a soil sample, intact decaying log or riverborne minerals.

entries.name: Renewing forest
entries.visualSubject: Small new fern trees with splayed divided fronds grow among taller trunks of the same early fern forest, their roots reaching into rich soil beside old naturally snapped and splintered trunks and decaying wood. Every broken trunk has an irregular torn end, with no flat saw-cut stump, axe marks, tools or broadleaf sapling replacing the fern family.
entries.distinction: Ordinary decay nourishes new members of the same fern-tree forest; splintered natural breaks exclude logging, and divided fronds exclude a modern broadleaf substitute or post-impact forest scene.

acceptableBlindMatches: new tree nourished by old wood
cycle of forest growth and decay

entries.name: Peat
entries.visualSubject: A cutaway of saturated dark brown ground exposes thick soft layers of recognizable pressed stems and leaves beneath a shallow mossy pool.
entries.distinction: Wet partly decomposed plant fibers remain visible, unlike crumbly topsoil, deep carbon seam or mineral sand.

entries.name: Buried carbon
entries.visualSubject: A deep dark carbon-rich layer containing faint compressed plant traces lies beneath several thick ochre sediment beds and far below a small green surface.
entries.distinction: Deep burial and a distinct dark organic seam; not exposed wet peat or repeated alternating iron bands.

entries.name: Forest rain
entries.visualSubject: The same tall early fern forest raises straight trunks into a canopy of splayed, clearly divided jade fronds; fine pale moisture wisps rise from that canopy into a low cloud that rains over the far edge of the forest. Keep the frond crowns distinct rather than replacing them with rounded flowering or broadleaf tree canopies.
entries.distinction: Moisture rises from the established fern-tree canopy before rain returns; the shared frond anatomy distinguishes this family from later flowering woodland, ordinary rainfall and the sea-land water cycle.

entries.name: Arthropods
entries.visualSubject: A dark ochre many-segmented shoreline animal has a clear external armored back, antennae and several pairs of visibly jointed legs.
entries.distinction: More than six jointed legs and external armor; insects have exactly six, vertebrates have four fleshy limbs.

entries.name: Insects
entries.visualSubject: One broad-bodied ochre insect stands in side-three-quarter view with exactly six clearly separated legs, two antennae and three main body regions; wings are folded or absent.
entries.distinction: Six-legged ground insect silhouette, without broad extended wings, many leg pairs or a dung ball.

entries.name: Winged insects
entries.visualSubject: A slim dragonfly-like insect spreads two pairs of translucent jade-veined wings above a six-legged body and long segmented abdomen.
entries.distinction: Four membranous insect wings with six legs and no vertebrate forelimb, feathers or bat fingers.

entries.name: Canopy life
entries.visualSubject: Three small six-legged winged insects move between broad leaves and branching twigs high above a barely visible forest floor, forming a lively horizontal band.
entries.distinction: Multiple insects inhabiting a leaf-and-branch layer, with no birds, bats or primate silhouettes.

entries.name: Air-breathing fish
entries.visualSubject: A broad-finned fish raises its mouth above the surface of a shallow reedless pool, its scaled body and fleshy paired fins still submerged among roots.
entries.distinction: Fish body at the air-water boundary; no four walking limbs, blowhole or mammal tail flukes.

entries.name: Limbed vertebrates
entries.visualSubject: A low long-tailed early tetrapod braces on four broad fleshy limbs at a muddy water margin, with splayed digits and a smooth continuous back.
entries.distinction: Four weight-bearing limbs with digits, not fin rays, segmented armor or the drier scaled reptile posture.

entries.name: Shelled egg
entries.visualSubject: A pale oval egg rests on dry ochre ground, with a clean small cutaway revealing protective membranes and a curled embryo inside; keep the shell otherwise whole.
entries.distinction: Large oval egg and curled animal embryo, distinct from sea shells, empty vesicles or plant seed cotyledons.

entries.name: Reptiles
entries.visualSubject: A medium dark-ochre lizard-like reptile stands firmly on four scaled limbs with a long tapering tail, dry ridged skin and a low angular head.
entries.distinction: Scaled dry-land body without fur, long sauropod neck or wet amphibian skin.

entries.name: Birds
entries.visualSubject: A small ochre-and-jade feathered bird perches on a bare twig with one wing partly open, showing layered flight feathers, a short beak and two feet.
entries.distinction: Feathered wing and two-legged perched body; no membrane fingers, insect limbs or migration group.

entries.name: Great browsers
entries.visualSubject: Two enormous sauropod-like plant eaters have long rising necks, small heads, barrel bodies, pillar legs and long tails; the nearer one strips foliage beside a tiny tree. An alternating paired trail combines large oval hind prints with smaller clawless horseshoe-shaped foreprints in the damp ground.
entries.distinction: Consistent long-necked reptile giants with large oval hind and smaller horseshoe-shaped foreprints; never horned mammals or predatory dinosaurs.

entries.name: Small furred animals
entries.visualSubject: Two small shrew-like mammals with pointed noses, round ears, long tails and fine ochre fur shelter beside a large fallen branch; their bodies remain alert and intact.
entries.distinction: Establish the recurring small-mammal ancestor before catastrophe; no frost coats, devastated backdrop or insect anatomy.

entries.name: Flowers
entries.visualSubject: Three simple coral and ochre flowers open on a leafy green stem, with broad petals and visible central pollen-bearing structures. Avoid a cut bouquet or decorative vase.
entries.distinction: Flower anatomy and attached living plant dominate, without visiting insect, developed fruit or recovery backdrop.

entries.name: Pollination
entries.visualSubject: One six-legged ochre insect bridges two open coral flowers, with a few visible pale pollen grains on its body and on the second flower's centre.
entries.distinction: Pollen transfer between two flowers is the action; the returning population icon includes young woodland and multiple visitors.

entries.name: Seeds
entries.visualSubject: Three plump ochre seeds lie together, one split to reveal a pale curled plant embryo and its stored food beneath a dark protective coat.
entries.distinction: Substantial seed bodies and plant embryo, without airborne dust, waiting through seasons or animal egg contents.

entries.name: Seedling
entries.visualSubject: One fresh jade seedling rises from a cracked ochre seed, showing two broad cotyledons above a short stem and a single fine root below.
entries.distinction: One complete germinating seed with paired seed leaves; green shoots are a survivor group among dead ground.

entries.name: Windborne seeds
entries.visualSubject: Three recognizable ochre seeds carry broad pale papery wings as they spiral away from a leafy branch, each heavy seed body distinct from its wing.
entries.distinction: Large winged seeds carried by air, not microscopic spores, deposited seeds or bird flight.

entries.name: Fruit
entries.visualSubject: A short living branch carries two plump coral fruits and one opened fruit showing several dark seeds inside its pale flesh.
entries.distinction: Ripe fleshy seed enclosure isolated as a branch; no recovery woodland or emphasis on a loose seed supply.

entries.name: Seed dispersal
entries.visualSubject: A small four-limbed animal carries a coral fruit away from its parent plant, while two intact dark seeds lie farther along its path on bare soil.
entries.distinction: Animal movement and separated seeds link fruit to new ground; no dung pile or generalized wind scatter.

acceptableBlindMatches: animal carrying fruit and spreading seeds

entries.name: Flowering forest
entries.visualSubject: Three established green tree crowns carry small coral blossoms and ochre fruit above a shaded floor, with one bird and one small mammal at different branches.
entries.distinction: Mature flower-and-fruit forest community before catastrophe, without young sapling rows, broken old trunks or giant-free recovery evidence.

entries.name: Axial tilt
entries.visualSubject: The same rocky planet retains its recognizable hook-shaped ochre continent and two smaller satellite ridges, now surrounded by jade sea; a single thin ivory polar axis passes through the planet on a clear diagonal against a faint horizontal orbital plane. A small rotation arc circles one planetary pole, while the land and sea remain exposed rather than replaced by gas-giant cloud swirls.
entries.distinction: Tilt belongs to the polar axis of the same rocky world, with recognizable solid land and jade sea; no gas-giant bands, axis through a Sun, symmetric magnetic loops or four seasonal views.

entries.name: Seasons
entries.visualSubject: Four recognizably seasonal views of the same forked branch form a loose ring around a golden Sun: fresh spring leaves, dense summer foliage, ochre autumn leaves falling and a bare snow-touched winter twig. The Sun is an ordinary clear disk with no axis, pole line or rotation arc through or around it.
entries.distinction: Four changing states of one branch around sunlight show the seasonal cycle; no line through the Sun that could suggest solar tilt causes seasons, counting record or single tipped globe.

entries.name: Mountain range
entries.visualSubject: A continuous serrated chain of three dark ochre mountains rises in overlapping ridges, with pale high peaks and a deep shadowed valley between them.
entries.distinction: Several linked ridges without erupting crater, broad U-shaped valley focus or a dominant ice tongue.

entries.name: Rain shadow
entries.visualSubject: One sharp mountain divides the circle: a jade cloud rains on its green windward slope while the far slope is bare ochre beneath clear sky; a thin air ribbon passes over the summit.
entries.distinction: Wet and dry sides of the same barrier are essential; no detached desert panorama or uniform mountain weather.

acceptableBlindMatches: wet and dry sides of a mountain

entries.name: Desert
entries.visualSubject: Broad ochre dunes curve around a patch of cracked stony ground beneath a small white sun, with deep indigo shadows and no water or green plants.
entries.distinction: Dry open land without wet refuge, grass cover or explanatory mountain comparison.

entries.name: Oasis
entries.visualSubject: A small jade spring-fed pool sits within ochre desert rock, ringed by several dense green shrubs and one spreading tree. The surrounding land remains dry.
entries.distinction: Isolated water and vegetation in arid ground, without arriving wildlife, grassland herd or extensive soaked ground.

entries.name: Grassland
entries.visualSubject: A broad stand of tall ochre and jade grasses sways across gently rolling open land, with two distinct seed heads in the foreground and no tree canopy.
entries.distinction: Grass habitat alone; no highlighted soil cycling, animals or bare dunes.

entries.name: Glacier
entries.visualSubject: A thick pale-blue glacier descends between two dark mountain ridges, its cracked ice tongue curving toward a moraine of loose rocks.
entries.distinction: Confined flowing mountain ice with cracks, not an expanding continental front, falling snow or ice-free carved valley.

entries.name: Valley
entries.visualSubject: A wide U-shaped ochre valley lies between steep rounded walls, with scraped bare rock and a small stream on the broad flat floor; no ice remains in the foreground.
entries.distinction: Glacially shaped open land trough, without deep sea, dominant ice tongue or repeatedly divided river channels.

entries.name: Braided river
entries.visualSubject: Several bright jade channels split and rejoin around pale gravel bars across a broad mountain valley, with cold blue headwaters visible in the distance.
entries.distinction: Repeated inland splits and joins over gravel; delta fans into sea and migration adds animals using the corridor.

entries.name: Grazing herds
entries.visualSubject: Three sturdy four-legged grazing animals with short necks, modest horns and dark hoofed feet bend over open grasses, their bodies smaller than the surrounding land.
entries.distinction: Short-necked herd animals and grazing posture; no sauropod necks, predator stance or pond gathering.

entries.name: Scent tracking
entries.visualSubject: The recurring small pointed-nosed mammal lowers its nose toward a faint ochre scent trail curling along the ground from an unseen animal, with its ears lifted and body following the trail.
entries.distinction: Nose and airborne trace guide the route; no remembered fruit destination or visually focused primate.

entries.name: Hunting mammals
entries.visualSubject: Two lean furred predators with alert pointed ears, forward eyes and flexible tails move low through grass; the nearer one pauses with its muzzle close to the ground.
entries.distinction: Larger predatory body and stalking posture, without visible prey confrontation or vulnerable ancestor shelter.

entries.name: Predator and prey
entries.visualSubject: A lean ochre mammal pursues a darker short-necked grazer across an open strip of grass, the prey turning away while the hunter extends forward. Keep clear space between them.
entries.distinction: Two different roles in an active pursuit, no gore and no diagram of broader nutrient connections.

entries.name: Dung
entries.visualSubject: A small irregular dark-brown pile of herbivore dung rests in grass, with visible short plant fibers and a few flies kept too small to dominate.
entries.distinction: Discrete organic droppings above the ground, not a soil cross-section or a beetle rolling a ball.

entries.name: Dung beetles
entries.visualSubject: One sturdy six-legged dark beetle pushes a round brown dung ball backward across ochre soil, its curved forelegs and hard wing cases clearly visible.
entries.distinction: Beetle-and-ball action is essential; no generic insect portrait or loose dung alone.

entries.name: Fertile grassland
entries.visualSubject: Strong jade grass tufts rise above a dark soil cutaway where a beetle burrow and broken-down dung feed a fine pale root network.
entries.distinction: Grass growth visibly linked to waste burial beneath it, not generic green field or forest nutrient return.

entries.name: Food web
entries.visualSubject: A compact grassland scene contains grass, a grazer, a lean hunter and a dung beetle, joined by broad unobtrusive ochre paths that return to the soil beneath the grass.
entries.distinction: Grassland feeding and nutrient relationships, not one chase, recovering woodland or a whole-world community map.

acceptableBlindMatches: grassland food chain and nutrient cycle

entries.name: Watering place
entries.visualSubject: Two short-necked grazers drink at a shallow jade pool while a lean hunter remains partly concealed in distant grass; hoofprints mark the wet edge.
entries.distinction: Shared grassland water draws herd and predator, rather than isolated desert grove or protected refuge.

entries.name: Far-ranging birds
entries.visualSubject: Three long-winged feathered birds fly above a sharp mountain saddle, their extended wings and differing distances forming one strong diagonal route.
entries.distinction: Feathered flock crossing mountain terrain; no phase cycle or insects.

entries.name: Seasonal journeys
entries.visualSubject: Two small groups of feathered birds traverse a long pale looping route between a leafy warm branch and a snow-touched bare branch, with land and water below.
entries.distinction: Recurring bird journey between seasonal habitats; river migration uses walking mammals and one ground corridor.

entries.name: Island life
entries.visualSubject: The established volcanic island now has a modest green canopy and two perched birds separated by a broad blue sea from a distant mainland edge.
entries.distinction: Living population isolated on the same island shape, without distinct call patterns or a bare cone.

entries.name: Different songs
entries.visualSubject: Two related feathered birds perch on separate island branches across a strip of sea; one sends three short pale sound arcs and the other a longer rising pair.
entries.distinction: Bird calls differ across separated populations; no humans, music notation or suggestion that insects became birds.

entries.name: Many-voiced world
entries.visualSubject: The hook-marked planet carries small distinct habitat patches at its rim: a forest bird, an island bird, a grazer and a canopy insect, each with a restrained outward ripple of sound.
entries.distinction: Whole pre-impact living world with several communities; no recovery stumps, ice margins or resurrected giants in later tokens.

acceptableBlindMatches: world full of animals and voices

entries.name: Impact winter
entries.visualSubject: The recurring planet is wrapped in a dark ash-grey veil that blocks most sunlight, with a small fading impact scar at its rim and a cold bare strip of land below.
entries.distinction: Sun-obscuring impact aftermath rather than collision itself, glacier growth or a local fallen woodland.

entries.name: Last tracks
entries.visualSubject: Exactly two alternating left-right sauropod step pairs cross grey ash-dusted wet mud and stop beneath an empty dark horizon: two large oval hind depressions each accompany a smaller clawless D-shaped foreprint, four impressions total. No living giant or approaching giant silhouette appears.
entries.distinction: Soft-ground paired walking tracks ending in a lifeless landscape, without circular crater rims; fossil tracks later become hardened rock impressions.

entries.name: Fossil footprints
entries.visualSubject: A long tilted dry ochre stone slab preserves the same two alternating left-right sauropod step pairs as Last tracks: two large oval hind depressions and two smaller clawless D-shaped foreprints, four impressions total. A chipped layered edge and small fern establish stone and scale without crater-like raised rims.
entries.distinction: Paired oval-and-horseshoe giant tracks fixed in stone, not circular craters, fresh muddy prints, three-toed carnivore tracks or living animals.

entries.name: Fallen forest
entries.visualSubject: Three broken dark tree trunks lie across grey ground beneath a dim sky, with one upright dead snag and only a tiny sheltered patch of green at the lower edge.
entries.distinction: Landscape-scale canopy loss, not one fallen branch or vigorous new woodland.

entries.name: Deadwood refuge
entries.visualSubject: The hollow underside of a fallen trunk shelters pale fungal threads, small invertebrates and two tiny pointed-nosed mammals, with damp dark ground protected beneath the wood.
entries.distinction: Habitat and decomposer food web dominate; the survivor icon gives the mammals central visual weight.

entries.name: Small survivors
entries.visualSubject: The same pair of pointed-nosed, round-eared small mammals crouches in the sheltered hollow of a large broken trunk, with fungi nearby and an ash-grey clearing beyond the entrance.
entries.distinction: Recognizable ancestral mammals foregrounded in post-impact shelter, with no new unrelated body plan or cold-coat comparison.

entries.name: Seed cache
entries.visualSubject: A shallow sheltered hollow beneath a log contains a tight cluster of intact ochre seeds; one familiar small mammal holds another seed at the entrance.
entries.distinction: Deliberately gathered store with an animal custodian, not a loose seed sample or dispersed trail.

acceptableBlindMatches: seeds hidden by a small mammal

entries.name: Green shoots
entries.visualSubject: Four tiny vivid jade shoots break through ash-grey soil beside a broken black branch, each emerging from a partly visible surviving seed.
entries.distinction: Multiple new shoots in damaged ground; no tall saplings, moss carpet or isolated clean germination diagram.

entries.name: Pioneer woodland
entries.visualSubject: A small uneven stand of young jade saplings grows among dark fallen logs, with mushrooms and rich soil at their roots and wide gaps between the new crowns.
entries.distinction: Recovery saplings share the frame with catastrophic deadwood; young grove is new establishment on open ground near the horizon.

entries.name: Returning pollinators
entries.visualSubject: Two clearly six-legged flying insects visit coral flowers on young saplings beside an old broken trunk; the small green canopy remains open.
entries.distinction: Returning insect population in recovery woodland, not a close pollen-transfer diagram or fruit-bearing branch.

entries.name: Returning fruit
entries.visualSubject: A young jade sapling beside a dark old stump bears a few plump coral fruits, one split enough to show seeds; a pollinating insect is small and secondary.
entries.distinction: Fruit attached to young recovery growth with old damage retained, rather than an isolated ripe branch.

acceptableBlindMatches: fruit on a young tree beside a stump

entries.name: Spreading mammals
entries.visualSubject: Three related furred mammals spread from a deadwood shelter into young woodland: a small pointed-nosed ancestor, a sturdier ground browser and a nimble branch-climber. Maintain shared ears, fur and four-limbed anatomy.
entries.distinction: Diversifying descendants of established small mammals across habitats, without suggesting their first origin after impact.

entries.name: Tree dwellers
entries.visualSubject: Two long-tailed primate-like mammals grip branching limbs with flexible hands and feet, one reaching toward a fruit while the other watches from above.
entries.distinction: Climbing furred vertebrates with grasping limbs, not insects, ground shrews or a warning-focused social scene.

entries.name: Whales
entries.visualSubject: A large streamlined jade-grey whale curves through deep water beside a smaller calf, showing horizontal tail flukes, small foreflippers and a short exhalation at the surface.
entries.distinction: Mammal body, calf and horizontal flukes, without fish scales, gills or insect wings.

entries.name: Bats
entries.visualSubject: One ochre-furred bat spreads broad dark-jade skin wings supported by long visible finger bones, with round ears, a small muzzle and two tiny hind feet.
entries.distinction: Fur and finger-supported membranes; no feathers, four separate insect wings or six legs.

entries.name: New food web
entries.visualSubject: Young woodland holds a pollinating insect, fruiting sapling, small mammal and lean furred hunter, connected by a few curved ochre feeding paths that pass through seeds and soil.
entries.distinction: Reconnected post-impact woodland relationships, with the familiar broken trunk beneath; no sauropod giants or grassland-only chain.

entries.name: Recovering world
entries.visualSubject: The familiar curved ochre world and hooked coastline support a mixed young forest with a small furred mammal and an insect pollinator at its living edge. Old naturally splintered, charred fallen wood remains among the different new growth as evidence of loss; no giant footprints, track depressions, fossil-track slab or living great browsers appear anywhere.
entries.distinction: A changed young ecosystem reconnects around old fallen wood, preserving loss without fresh giant tracks; no retreating ice front or restored browsing giants.

acceptableBlindMatches: renewed ecosystems with traces of loss

entries.name: Snowfall
entries.visualSubject: Broad pale snow crystals and soft flakes fall from a cold jade-grey cloud onto the upper surface of a mountain glacier, accumulating as a fresh white cap.
entries.distinction: Falling flakes and new snow layer dominate, not rain streaks or an outward-moving thick ice front.

entries.name: Advancing ice
entries.visualSubject: A thick blue-white ice front spreads outward from high mountains across an ochre valley, burying low ridges and pushing a dark moraine before its steep cracked edge.
entries.distinction: Outward expansion of sustained glacial ice, with no ash veil or receding green margin.

entries.name: River migration
entries.visualSubject: A mixed line of small mammals and hoofed grazers follows a jade river downhill away from snowy peaks toward green lower country; the river remains the clear connecting route.
entries.distinction: Ground wildlife moves along a river corridor during climate change; no bird loop or one animal's remembered fruit route.

entries.name: Sheltered oasis
entries.visualSubject: Several small mammals and a short-necked grazer gather beneath a dense green grove around a jade spring, protected by ochre rock while distant blue ice remains outside the warm enclosure.
entries.distinction: A reached climate refuge with varied travellers and distant ice, not an empty oasis or one hiding primate.

entries.name: Varied survivors
entries.visualSubject: Four members of the established small shrew-like mammal lineage stand together on neutral ground, each retaining a pointed snout, round ears, a low four-legged body and a visibly long slender tail extending beyond its rump. Their coats vary from thin through dense to softly shaggy while the body plan stays the same; thick fur has no quills, spikes or hedgehog dome.
entries.distinction: Existing variation in soft coat thickness within one long-tailed, pointed-snouted lineage; no quills, hedgehog anatomy, lost tails, sudden individual transformation or universal white coat.

entries.name: Cold-adapted populations
entries.visualSubject: Three thick-soft-furred descendants of the same shrew-like mammals forage beside snow and low sheltering rocks, including one smaller juvenile. All retain clearly pointed snouts, round ears and visibly long slender tails beyond their thick coats, without quills, spikes, hedgehog bodies or short hidden tails.
entries.distinction: A reproducing population of the established long-tailed mammals with dense soft fur in cold habitat; no unrelated hedgehog-like replacement or one animal growing an instant winter coat.

acceptableBlindMatches: furry mammals with young in cold habitat

entries.name: Surviving lineages
entries.visualSubject: Two small family groups occupy adjoining habitats divided by a rock ridge: thin-furred shrew-like mammals beside a green spring and thick-soft-furred relatives beside lingering snow, each with a juvenile. Every individual retains the same pointed snout, round ears and conspicuous long slender tail, making related lineages visible across the two settings without quills or hedgehog anatomy.
entries.distinction: Warm-refuge and cold-habitat families remain recognizable relatives through shared pointed snouts, round ears and long tails; soft fur differs, not the underlying animal body plan.

entries.name: World after the ice
entries.visualSubject: The same curved world retains its hook-shaped ochre land and jade water, with ice withdrawn to the far high horizon, a free-flowing river and restored woodland spreading over open lower ground among small mammals. A little old fallen wood remains within the changed forest, but no giant footprints, track depressions or living great browsers appear.
entries.distinction: Distant retreated ice, a reopened river and restored woodland identify the post-glacial world; the same geography persists without any fresh tracks implying returned giant browsers.

entries.name: Attention
entries.visualSubject: A close profile of the established long-tailed tree dweller leans toward a bright coral fruit, its wide dark eye and lifted grasping hand aligned with the object.
entries.distinction: Focused living gaze at a nearby target, not an isolated eye, recoiling danger response or human looking at stars.

entries.name: Fear
entries.visualSubject: The same tree dweller crouches backward on a branch, gripping it tightly while a small lean predator silhouette appears below; the animal's eye is wide and tail drawn close.
entries.distinction: Visible defensive response to a perceived threat, rather than active hunting or a relaxed hidden animal.

entries.name: Safety
entries.visualSubject: The tree dweller rests with a smaller companion inside a dense sheltered green grove, hidden behind interlocking branches while a distant predator passes outside the foliage.
entries.distinction: Concealment from a specific danger and relaxed posture, not a broad climate refuge or an alarm exchange.

entries.name: Memory
entries.visualSubject: The tree dweller studies a familiar forked fruit branch; a faint second ivory outline of that same branch appears behind its head, while the real branch remains solid jade and coral. This double image is the recurring convention for remembered experience.
entries.distinction: One present object paired with a faint matching recollection, not a route, general gaze or sound passed between people.

acceptableBlindMatches: memory represented by a repeated image

entries.name: Learned path
entries.visualSubject: A single tree dweller follows an ochre path around a dark ridge toward a fruiting tree partly hidden beyond it; a faint pale trace of the same route sits under its feet.
entries.distinction: One familiar route to a destination not visible from the starting point; no mass climate migration or seed carrying.

entries.name: Call
entries.visualSubject: The tree dweller opens its mouth from a high branch, releasing three broad pale sound arcs into clear air while one companion remains partly hidden behind distant leaves.
entries.distinction: Single animal signal radiates outward without a returning wall reflection, human exchange or different bird motifs.

entries.name: Shared warning
entries.visualSubject: One tree dweller calls from a branch while two companions turn sharply toward the same partly hidden predator; pale sound arcs link caller and listeners.
entries.distinction: Signal visibly changes several listeners' attention toward a threat; no solitary cry or calm group portrait.

acceptableBlindMatches: group responding to a warning call

entries.name: Social group
entries.visualSubject: Four established ochre-furred, long-tailed tree dwellers share a sheltered branch network as an animal family: one grooms a companion, another keeps watch and a smaller juvenile stays close. Preserve their primate faces, grasping hands and feet, full body fur and visibly curling tails; there are no humans, clothes or tools.
entries.distinction: Care, grooming and shared vigilance among the same furred long-tailed animal family, not a clothed human family, human conversation, specific alarm or simple climbing pair.

entries.name: Language
entries.visualSubject: Two human figures in profile face one another with open speaking mouths and different deliberate hand gestures, while a third follows their shared gaze toward a small carved-free stone and the Moon.
entries.distinction: Reciprocal human symbolic communication, not one animal call, storytelling scene or evidence review; no text, speech bubbles or alphabet.

entries.name: Story
entries.visualSubject: A seated human narrator gestures to two listeners; behind the moving hand, a soft ochre vignette shows a small animal travelling beneath a crescent Moon, clearly separate from the present ground.
entries.distinction: Narration evokes an imagined or remembered sequence in open space, not a painted wall, book or direct lesson at the shore.

entries.name: Constellations
entries.visualSubject: Seven ivory stars form a loose animal-like pattern across ultramarine darkness, joined by a few fine ochre lines; unrelated background stars remain unconnected.
entries.distinction: Selected stars connected into a pattern, not every star linked, a painted rock surface or counting device.

entries.name: Calendar
entries.visualSubject: A human observer crouches beside four small groups of counting pebbles and incised tally strokes on a natural stone, beneath a repeated star pattern shown at four seasonal positions around a single horizon.
entries.distinction: Deliberate record of recurring sky and season, not a modern calendar page, clock or mere cycle of leaves.

entries.name: Wonder
entries.visualSubject: A small human figure stands on the hooked shore with head tipped far back and both arms gently open beneath a vast cluster of luminous stars; the upward gaze dominates.
entries.distinction: Receptive astonishment at the sky, without a pointing exchange, counting marks or joined stellar figure.

entries.name: Question
entries.visualSubject: One human figure extends an open palm toward a small bright Moon while turning an expectant face toward another person; the other person's hand pauses above the empty space between them.
entries.distinction: An unresolved shared inquiry shown by reciprocal pose and open space, without written question marks or a proposed sky-sea connection.

entries.name: Lunar rhythm
entries.visualSubject: Two matching views of the same hooked shore profile show calm water beneath a full Moon in the upper view and a quarter Moon with exactly half its disk lit in the lower view.
