Each view contains exactly two clear static horizontal water-level marks against the same rock face: widely separated high and low levels for the full Moon, closely spaced high and low levels for the quarter Moon; no surf or wave-height difference carries the comparison.
entries.distinction: Moon phase accompanies a broad versus narrow high-to-low tidal range at identical shore geometry, expressed by two static level marks per view; not wave amplitude, storm size, a lone tide height or a solitary crescent.

entries.name: Lunar hypothesis
entries.visualSubject: A human observer points one hand toward the pale Moon and the other toward two tidal bands on the familiar hooked shore; one fine tentative ochre arc joins those observed features.
entries.distinction: A proposed connection is the foreground action, without future date markers or measured confirmation; the arc is a visual conjecture convention.

entries.name: Spring-tide prediction
entries.visualSubject: Beside the familiar shore, a person sets two pale dry ochre marks far apart on a rock face while indicating an outlined future full Moon above a short pebble count; the present sea remains between the marks.
entries.distinction: Dry proposed upper and lower limits and a future full-Moon cue, not an already wet verified tide record.

acceptableBlindMatches: marking expected high and low tides

entries.name: Observed spring tide
entries.visualSubject: At the same marked shore, one observer compares a clear dark high-water stain with the newly exposed low-water edge below it; the widely separated ochre marks now align with those two observed levels beneath a full Moon.
entries.distinction: Actual wet stain and exposed low water establish a checked range; keep the prediction rock and marks identical.

acceptableBlindMatches: tide prediction tested at the shore

entries.name: Shared discovery
entries.visualSubject: Three people stand at the same marked tidal rock; one indicates the high-water stain and low-water edge while another compares the pebble record and a third looks between the evidence and Moon.
entries.distinction: Peers share a tested observation and its record, without a single observer or an adult-to-child lesson.

entries.name: Night vision
entries.visualSubject: A nocturnal furred animal's large forward eyes reflect pale moonlight above a dark branch, with its whiskered face and the branch still readable in a nearly black jade setting.
entries.distinction: Paired low-light eyes in an active nocturnal animal, not the Moon granting vision or one isolated marine eye.

entries.name: Pigment
entries.visualSubject: Three small wet daubs of ochre, coral and dark mineral color sit on a flat natural stone beside a crushed mineral fragment and a short watery smear.
entries.distinction: Prepared wet coloring material, without a vessel, modern palette, loose soil or completed picture.

entries.name: Cave painting
entries.visualSubject: The established sea cave's dry pale upper wall bears one simple ochre animal outline and a hand stencil, with a human hand adding a broad mark; the dark wave-washed entrance remains below.
entries.distinction: Clearly handmade picture on dry rock depicting a plausible animal, not a real creature, fossil or celestial mural.

acceptableBlindMatches: animal painted on a cave wall

entries.name: Imagined beast
entries.visualSubject: On the same dry cave wall, an ochre painted creature combines a long-tailed mammal body, branching antlers and feathered wings in one impossible silhouette; a small painter's hand remains at the edge.
entries.distinction: Impossible anatomy is visibly a painting, never a resurrected sauropod or a newly living lineage.

acceptableBlindMatches: impossible animal on a cave wall
winged antlered creature in rock art

entries.name: Echo
entries.visualSubject: A lone human calls inside the established sea cave; one pale sound arc travels toward the curved dry wall and a fainter matching arc returns toward the caller, with the sea visible through the lower opening.
entries.distinction: Opposing original and reflected sound paths in the same rocky chamber, not multiple singers or a composed melodic pattern.

entries.name: Song
entries.visualSubject: One human singer in the dry upper cave chamber releases a repeating sequence of three broad pale sound arcs, with the last arc rising and the singer's hand marking a gentle pulse.
entries.distinction: Deliberately repeated human phrase rather than a single alarm or reflected copy; no musical notes or staff.

entries.name: Chorus
entries.visualSubject: Three human singers of different heights face inward on the dry cave ledge, their mouths open and three separate pale sound ribbons meeting in one repeating arc above them.
entries.distinction: Several people singing together, with distinct contributors and shared pattern; no written music or speech bubbles.

entries.name: Painted sky
entries.visualSubject: The same dry pale cave wall carries a bold ultramarine patch filled with oversized ochre stars, an impossible coral spiral and a pale crescent; a painted handprint marks the lower edge.
entries.distinction: Clearly pigment on rock with deliberately impossible celestial arrangement, not a natural starfield or an astronomical record.

entries.name: Teaching
entries.visualSubject: An older person traces the familiar Moon-and-tide pattern in sand beside the marked shore while two younger listeners follow the hand; their faces and hands form a close triangle around the evidence.
entries.distinction: Knowledge passed across generations using the already tested shore, not a modern classroom, book or peer-only discussion.

entries.name: New question
entries.visualSubject: A young learner lifts an open hand toward a different star beyond the Moon-and-tide pattern in the sand while an older teacher pauses and turns to follow the new direction.
entries.distinction: The learner extends inquiry beyond the received pattern; no question mark, certificate or passive reception.

entries.name: Remembered song
entries.visualSubject: One younger singer repeats a three-arc pale vocal pattern; behind the singer sits a faint matching outline of an earlier group of singers and the same three arcs, without ghostly faces.
entries.distinction: Inherited repeated phrase and memory convention, not resurrected people or an altered ending.

entries.name: Changed song
entries.visualSubject: A young singer repeats the first two ivory arcs of the inherited vocal phrase, then sends its third arc into a distinct rising coral curl; a faint old third arc stays lower behind it.
entries.distinction: Preserve the opening motif and visibly change only the ending; no printed notes or arbitrary entirely new pattern.

acceptableBlindMatches: altered ending of an inherited song

entries.name: Children's chorus
entries.visualSubject: Three children of visibly different small heights sing together on the cave's dry ledge, sharing the inherited two ivory arcs and the new rising coral ending; a taller adult listens at the far edge.
entries.distinction: Children collectively perform the changed motif, rather than adult chorus, solo revision or spoken lesson.

entries.name: Dormant seeds
entries.visualSubject: Three intact dark-coated seeds rest protected beneath a curled dry leaf and a thin layer of cold soil, while a pale frost edge lies above them; no root has emerged.
entries.distinction: Living seeds waiting through unfavorable conditions, not stored food cache, dead grains or active germination.

entries.name: Scattered seeds
entries.visualSubject: Several familiar dark-coated seeds lie well separated across new ochre ground, with one near an animal footprint and another beneath a distant fruit branch; none has sprouted yet.
entries.distinction: Arrived seeds spread across multiple places, not winged airborne seeds, carrying action or one sheltered cluster.

entries.name: Young grove
entries.visualSubject: Four fresh jade saplings of differing heights establish on an open ochre slope, with visible seed coats at one root and clear space between their small crowns.
entries.distinction: New grove on open ground with no catastrophe logs; larger than a seedling and smaller than a distant established forest.

entries.name: Forest beyond the horizon
entries.visualSubject: A near grove releases a few small winged seeds toward a distant green ridge where additional young tree crowns disappear beyond the circle's far curve; a small open human hand remains low at the edge.
entries.distinction: Continuing establishment beyond view dominates, with the hand releasing rather than arranging; no living great browsers or final perfection emblem.

acceptableBlindMatches: forest growing beyond an open hand

productionAttention.check: Use oval hind and smaller horseshoe foreprints in alternating pairs; compare against Moon craters. Correct anatomy takes precedence over forcing instant dinosaur recognition.
Abstract chemistry conventions need strong different compositions at 64 px. Do not imply that color or a generic grain shape alone identifies an element or molecule.
Keep single body, division waist, enclosed partner, loose rosette and integrated ribbon distinct. Do not introduce a compulsory nucleus in early cells.
Use canopy height, trunk damage, young versus mature growth and habitat arrangement; avoid relying only on a greener palette.
One hooked coastal cave retains a wave-washed lower entrance and genuinely dry upper ledge/wall. Check both close icon and wider background views.

The same tide rock and upper/lower marks anchor inference, prospective range and observation. At small size these are context-assisted scenes; test whether the dry-to-wet evidence distinction survives.
Freeze the sound and memory motif before subsequent reviews. Judge solo, remembered, altered ending and child group as contextual distinctions; do not claim exact blind semantic recognition.
